headline: Request to abate $7,000 in property taxes at 209 Patchen Road heard; written decision due in 30 days.
summary: The Patchen Road applicant asks that the $7,000 tax bill for 2024-2025 be abated, with a payment plan for the rest. The tax collector said the account owes $8,334 in penalty, interest, and principal, and almost $16,000 in total to become current. A second hearing covered seven properties, including 165 Park Road, and a request to waive penalties on late taxes, with $1,955.88 owed in penalty and interest. Written decisions on both are due within 30 days.
discussion: Patchen Road tax abatement: Members asked why the state homestead credit was missing for 2024-2025 and whether a payment plan could cover the rest of the balance.

Tax sale process: The tax collector said the property could be auctioned in late winter or early spring if no payment plan is set up, and the owner would then have a year to reclaim it by paying back taxes, interest, and fees.

Park Road late-tax penalty: The owner said the envelope was mailed at a post office box on Saturday but was postmarked the 17th of March, one day after the 16th due date. The tax collector said payments must be postmarked by the due date to count as on time.
